newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares end more than one percent higher.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares end more than one percent higher.

text.p: 1540 GMT - Swiss shares ended more than one percent higher after a steady rise, profiting from a strong Wall Street and firming bonds futures.

The market was expecting the U.S. Fed to raise interest rates by 25 basis points at today's FOMC meeting, one dealer said. Volume was described as low ahaed of the long Easter holiday weekend. Further development was seen depending on the outcome of today's Fed meeting.
* Blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 61.3 points or 1.36 percent to 4,558.6 points.
* Broad SPI up 31.18 points or 1.09 percent to 2,887.96.

* CS Group and Novartis were among the biggest gainers. CS Group powered ahead 6.50 francs, or 3.9 percent, to end at 173. Novartis registereds, up 46 francs to 1,760, were reportedly bolstered by switches from Roche.
* Roche was easier after announcing a 16 percent rise in 1996 net profit to 3.899 billion Swiss francs on Monday.

* Nestle climbed six francs to 1,577. The company is due to release 1996 results on Wednesday. According to market consensus, Nestle is likely to report a net profit increase of 10.5 percent to around 3.23 billion Swiss francs.
* Several stocks were seen making up for recent losses. Among them were insurers Swiss Re and Zurich and temporary employment group Adecco, which added between two and three percent.
* Stocks of goods inspection firm Surveillance continued their recent fall, giving up 80 francs to 2,950. The shares were pulled down by a sell recommendation, traders said.
* Alusuisse, Holderbank and Winterthur were also among the losers.
* Trade on Swiss Options and Financial Futures (Soffex) was quiet and volume was low.

Dealers said activity was mostly reduced to position squaring. Volume in SMI futures, where 4,061 contracts changed hands, was bolstered by late short covering ahead of the Fed's FOMC meeting, one trader noted. The April SMI added 61 points to 4,568.
On the options side, total volume stood at 96,476 contracts, of which UBS options accounted for about a fifth. Options of Nestle and CS Group also saw some interest.
